news.title: Morocco PM warns football chief over 2030 World Cup final
news.lede: Morocco’s Prime Minister, Aziz Akhannouch, has warned the country’s football federation president, Fouzi Lekjaa, against making promises about hosting the 2030 World Cup final before discussions with co-hosts Spain and Portugal. The 2030 men’s World Cup will be jointly hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal, with the opening three matches taking place in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay as part of celebrations marking the tournament’s centenary. Although a proposed list of host stadiums has been drawn up, FIFA has yet to confirm the final venues or where the tournament’s showpiece match will be played. Lekjaa, president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (RMFF), had said at a political party event that Casablanca would have the “honour” of hosting the final.

news.title: 2030 World Cup final war intensifies after Morocco PM slams own federation chief and Spain fires back | Football News
news.lede: Moroccan Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch has publicly rebuked the country’s football federation president Fouzi Lekjaa over his claim that Morocco will host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final, warning that such a decision cannot be announced before discussions with co-hosts Spain and Portugal. The controversy erupted after Lekjaa said that the province of Benslimane, near Casablanca, would have the honour of staging the final. FIFA, however, has not yet announced the venue for the title clash, leaving the three principal host nations — Morocco, Spain and Portugal — to jostle for the showpiece game.Akhannouch made his displeasure clear during a rally ahead of elections in Morocco later this month, accusing Lekjaa of making a promise on an issue that remains unresolved.

news.title: 'Stop making promises!' - Moroccan PM steps in after football boss claims 2030 World Cup final

news.title: Spain’s Football Chief Dismisses World Cup Withdrawal Talk Amid 2030 Final Debate
news.lede: Rabat – Spanish Football Federation President Rafael Louzán has dismissed reports suggesting that Spain could withdraw from hosting the 2030 FIFA World Cup if Morocco is awarded the tournament’s final. Speaking to Spanish radio station Cadena COPE, Louzán said there was no basis for claims that Spain could pull out of the joint hosting project. He stressed that the tournament is governed by formal agreements signed by the parties involved. These agreements include Spain, Portugal, Morocco, FIFA, and the Spanish government, according to the official source.
